messages.author: edd4914c326b6d31
messages.subject: rstan interface for init
parts:
I tried this:
> myinit <- function(chainid) initv7[[chainid]]
> system.time(sflist <- mclapply(1:3, function(i) stan(model_code=stan_model, data=stanDat, iter=2000, chains=1,
+ init=myinit,
+ seed=seed, chain_id=i, refresh=-1,
+ warmup=500, thin=1,
+ control=list(adapt_engaged=FALSE,
+ stepsize=0.0015, max_treedepth=13)),
+ mc.cores=3)
+ )

....
Error in initv7[[chainid]] : invalid subscript type 'symbol'

The docs say that if init is a function "The function can take an
optional parameter ‘chain_id’".

I think the immediate problem is that the argument is named chain_id,
and so my argument, chainid, is simply undefined (not quite sure why it
should be type symbol--I guess chainid unbound is a symbol). Perhaps
the documentation could be clearer. Perhaps I should have realized what
it meant the first time :)

A more serious problem is that the rstan code, in misc.R, function
config_argss (sic), has
if (!inits_specified && is.function(init)) {
## the function can take an argument named by chain_id
if (any(names(formals(init)) == "chain_id")) {
inits <- lapply(1:chains, function(id) init(chain_id = id))
} else {
inits <- lapply(1:chains, function(id) init())
}

I think, since each of my 3 parallel jobs has only 1 chain, this means
the function will be invoked with chain_id=1 3 times.

Is this understanding correct?

I guess I could invoke the function like init=myinit(i) to get what I
want.

It seems unfortunate that the init function argument chain_id does not
correspond to the chain_id argument of the stan function. Generally,
the interface to init does not seem well-designed for parallel
application, in particular getting reproducible but independent random
number streams.

Ross Boylan

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan interface for init
parts:
Thanks.  You are right.  That piece of code is written before we think about using mcapply to simulate chains by parallel.  Given the current problem, you should generate the initial values before call stan() and pass them to stan(), which actually gives you better control and easiness on coding.

I will think about making it use the chain_id that is used for sampling.  But I do not want it to be too complicated as there are too many arguments for function to stan(); I would rather keep it simple even in terms of coding.

--
Jiqiang
